chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin, from Ubaydullah al-Wassaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
'To feed a Muslim man is more beloved to me than to free an 'Ufqa from the people.' I said, 'And how much is an 'Ufqa?' He said, 'Ten thousand.'

key_terms.أُفُقًا: a unit of value or slave, equivalent to ten thousand

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of feeding a Muslim compared to freeing slaves?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elevates the spiritual merit of sustaining a believer through food above the significant act of manumitting slaves, quantifying the latter as equivalent to ten thousand 'Ufqa. This comparison highlights the immediate, tangible impact of charity on the dignity and well-being of the individual in Shia ethical tradition, prioritizing direct sustenance over broader but less personal acts of liberation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muqarrin, from Ubeydullah Al Wassafy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If I were to feed a Muslim man, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to free an ‘Afqa’ from the people’. I said, ‘And how may is the ‘Afqa’?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ten thousand’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Muqrin from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Wassafi from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Feeding a Muslim man is more beloved to me than setting free a horizon (full) of people.’ I then asked, ‘How many is a horizon of people?’ The Imam said, ‘It is ten thousand people.’”
